description: A hierarchical file packaging format for the storage and transfer of arbitrary digital content. A bag consists of a payload (the content) and tag files (metadata about the content). Designed to support disk-based or network-based storage and transfer of digital content.

entities.name: Bag
entities.description: A bag is a base directory containing a set of tag files and a payload directory (data/). The base directory may have any name. A bag is complete when every element in every payload manifest and tag manifest is present, and valid when additionally all checksums match.
entities.note: A bag MUST contain bagit.txt, at least one payload manifest, and the data/ directory.

entities.name: Bag Declaration
entities.description: The bagit.txt file, which MUST be present in every bag. Contains exactly two lines declaring the BagIt version and the tag file character encoding. Must be encoded in UTF-8 without BOM.
entities.note: REQUIRED. Must be named 'bagit.txt'. Must be encoded in UTF-8. Must contain exactly two lines.

entities.name: Payload
entities.description: The data/ directory containing the actual digital content being packaged. All payload files MUST reside under this directory. Files are treated as opaque octet streams with no size limitations.
entities.note: REQUIRED. Must be named 'data/'. May contain arbitrary subdirectory structures.

entities.name: Payload File
entities.description: An individual file within the data/ payload directory. Every payload file MUST be listed in every payload manifest with its checksum.

entities.name: Payload Directory
entities.description: A subdirectory within the data/ payload directory. Directories themselves are not listed in manifests; only files are listed.
entities.note: Can nest recursively. Only files (not directories) appear in manifests.

entities.name: Manifest
entities.description: A payload manifest file listing the checksum and path of every file in the payload directory. At least one manifest MUST be present. Named manifest-ALGORITHM.txt (e.g., manifest-sha256.txt). Each line has format: CHECKSUM FILEPATH.
entities.note: REQUIRED (at least one). Starting with BagIt 1.0, implementations MUST support SHA-256 and SHA-512, and SHOULD enable SHA-512 by default. Must list every payload file exactly once.

entities.name: Manifest Entry
entities.description: A single line in a payload manifest. Contains the hex-encoded checksum and the file path relative to the bag base directory. The checksum is case-insensitive. Special characters in the filepath (LF, CR, CRLF, %) must be percent-encoded per RFC 3986.

entities.name: Tag Manifest
entities.description: An optional manifest for tag files (files outside the data/ directory). Named tagmanifest-ALGORITHM.txt. Same format as payload manifests. Must list every payload manifest. Should list remaining tag files except other tag manifests.
entities.note: OPTIONAL. Cannot reference payload files. Tag manifest filepaths never begin with 'data/'.

entities.name: Tag Manifest Entry
entities.description: A single line in a tag manifest. Contains the hex-encoded checksum and the file path of a tag file relative to the bag base directory.

entities.name: Bag Info
entities.description: The bag-info.txt file containing metadata elements about the bag as key-value pairs. All metadata elements are optional and most are repeatable. Labels are case-insensitive. Long values may be continued on the next line with leading whitespace.
entities.note: OPTIONAL. Labels cannot contain colons, LF, or CR. Recommended max 79 characters per line. Arbitrary additional metadata elements are permitted.

entities.name: Fetch File
entities.description: The fetch.txt file listing payload files that can be retrieved from remote locations instead of being included directly in the bag. Enables incomplete or 'holey' bags for transfer. Each line has three space-separated fields: URL LENGTH FILEPATH.
entities.note: OPTIONAL. All files listed in fetch.txt MUST also appear in every payload manifest. Cannot list tag files. Only absolute URIs per RFC 3986 are allowed.

entities.name: Fetch Entry
entities.description: A single line in fetch.txt. Contains the URL from which the file can be retrieved, its expected length (or '-' if unknown), and the file path where it should be placed relative to the bag base directory.

entities.name: Other Tag Files
entities.description: Arbitrary additional tag files created by implementers. May be in any format and placed in the bag base directory or in tag subdirectories. Their contents are otherwise ignored by BagIt processing unless listed in a tag manifest.
entities.note: OPTIONAL. If listed in a tag manifest, must pass checksum validation. Tag directories may be used to organize additional tag files.

checksumAlgorithms.md5: MD5 message digest (manifest-md5.txt). Widely supported but not recommended for new bags.
checksumAlgorithms.sha1: SHA-1 secure hash (manifest-sha1.txt). Supported but not recommended for new bags.
checksumAlgorithms.sha256: SHA-256 secure hash (manifest-sha256.txt). MUST be supported by BagIt 1.0 implementations.
checksumAlgorithms.sha512: SHA-512 secure hash (manifest-sha512.txt). MUST be supported by BagIt 1.0 implementations. SHOULD be enabled by default.

requiredFiles.bagit.txt: BagIt version and tag file character encoding declaration. REQUIRED in every bag.
requiredFiles.data/: Payload directory containing all digital content. REQUIRED in every bag.
requiredFiles.manifest-ALGORITHM.txt: Payload manifest with checksum for every payload file. At least one REQUIRED.

optionalFiles.bag-info.txt: Metadata about the bag as key-value pairs. OPTIONAL.
optionalFiles.tagmanifest-ALGORITHM.txt: Manifest with checksums for tag files. OPTIONAL.
optionalFiles.fetch.txt: List of URLs for remote payload files. OPTIONAL.

Organization-Address.description: Mailing address of the source organization

Contact-Name.description: Person at the source organization responsible for the content transfer

Contact-Phone.description: International format telephone number of the contact person

Contact-Email.description: Fully qualified email address of the contact person

External-Description.description: Brief explanation of the contents and provenance

Bagging-Date.description: Date the content was prepared for transfer, in YYYY-MM-DD format per RFC 3339

Bag-Size.description: Approximate size of the bag, intended for human consumption (e.g., '260 MB', '5.2 GB')

Payload-Oxum.description: The payload octet stream sum in format 'OctetCount.StreamCount' where OctetCount is total bytes and StreamCount is total number of payload files

Bag-Group-Identifier.description: A unique name given to a set of bags that together form a logical group

Bag-Count.description: Sequence number within a bag group in format 'N of T' (e.g., '1 of 15'). Use '?' for unknown total.

Internal-Sender-Identifier.description: An alternate sender-specific identifier for the content being transferred

Internal-Sender-Description.description: A sender-local explanation of the contents and provenance

bagStructure.baseDirectory: The top-level directory of the bag, which may have any name
bagStructure.payloadDirectory: data/ — REQUIRED directory containing all payload files
bagStructure.tagDirectory: Any directory at the top level other than data/, used for organizing additional tag files

completeness: At least one payload manifest exists
Every file listed in every payload manifest is present
Every file listed in every tag manifest is present
Every payload file appears in every payload manifest
No tag file appears in a payload manifest
No payload file appears in a tag manifest
validity: Every checksum in every payload manifest matches the corresponding file
Every checksum in every tag manifest matches the corresponding file

fileNamingRules.reservedNames: bagit.txt, bag-info.txt, fetch.txt are reserved tag file names
fileNamingRules.pathSeparator: Filepaths in manifests and fetch.txt MUST use '/' (forward slash) as separator
fileNamingRules.percentEncoding: LF, CR, CRLF, and % in filepaths must be percent-encoded per RFC 3986

serialization.zip: ZIP archive of the bag base directory
serialization.tar: TAR archive of the bag base directory

bagItVersions.1.0: Current version as defined in RFC 8493 (October 2018)
